source_text: The following remarks are obsolete as they are subsumed in Homology, Lemmas <REF_0001> and <REF_0002>. Let <MATH_0001> be an abelian category. Let <MATH_0002> be a weak Serre subcategory (see Homology, Definition <REF_0003>). Suppose that <MATH_0003> is a double complex to which Homology, Lemma <REF_0004> applies such that for some <MATH_0004> all the objects <MATH_0005> belong to <MATH_0006>. Then all the cohomology groups <MATH_0007> belong to <MATH_0008>. Namely, the assumptions imply that the kernels and images of <MATH_0009> are in <MATH_0010>. Whereupon we see that each <MATH_0011> is in <MATH_0012>. By induction we see that each <MATH_0013> is in <MATH_0014>. Hence each <MATH_0015> has a finite filtration whose subquotients are in <MATH_0016>. Using that <MATH_0017> is closed under extensions we conclude that <MATH_0018> is in <MATH_0019> as claimed. The same result holds for the second spectral sequence associated to <MATH_0020>. Similarly, if <MATH_0021> is a filtered complex to which Homology, Lemma <REF_0005> applies and for some <MATH_0022> all the objects <MATH_0023> belong to <MATH_0024>, then each <MATH_0025> is an object of <MATH_0026>.
